name: Two Harbours
tagline: A guest house between two harbours, on the island of Scalpay.
location: Scalpay · Isle of Harris · Outer Hebrides

hero.title: Between two harbours, the world can wait.
hero.intro: A granite-walled Victorian house, three en-suite rooms and a Hebridean welcome. Stay on Scalpay, with Harris and Lewis close at hand.
hero.alt: Two Harbours Guest House beside its mature garden, with the North Harbour and Harris hills beyond.
hero.caption: The Old Manse, between Scalpay’s North and South Harbours

statement.title: Three rooms. A large garden. Nothing you do not need.
paragraphs: Two Harbours is a thoughtfully renovated Victorian house between the two harbours of Scalpay. Expect modern comforts, historic charm and a personal meet-and-greet when you arrive.
Breakfast is freshly prepared in the farmhouse kitchen from locally sourced produce. In the evening, an optional lite-bite menu, wine and beer are there if you would rather stay in.

roomsIntro.title: Harbour light or garden quiet.
roomsIntro.text: Luskentyre and Scarista are larger, superior rooms with harbour views. Borve looks over the mature garden towards the South Harbour. All three have private en-suite shower rooms and can be arranged as a superking or twin when reserved.

houseIntro.eyebrow: A house with a long memory
houseIntro.title: Hospitality here is older than the house.
houseIntro.text: The present house was rebuilt in the 1880s, incorporating the ruins and foundations of an earlier farmstead. It was a draper’s and grocer’s, then a church manse. Before that, on this same site, Donald Campbell gave Bonnie Prince Charlie four nights of refuge in 1746.
houseIntro.quote: He came to me for safety, so how can I betray him.
houseIntro.attribution: Donald Campbell, as quoted in the house history

islandIntro.title: Cross the bridge. Keep the view.
islandIntro.text: Scalpay is connected to Harris by bridge. The house is a seven-mile scenic drive from Tarbert, the ferry port and hub of Harris—about ten minutes by car. The Harris beaches from Luskentyre to Scarista are around twenty minutes from Tarbert.

closing.title: Make one good decision.
closing.text: Choose your dates and book directly with the house. Breakfast is included; the harbours are already there.

rooms.title: A room for the way you wake.
rooms.intro: Three individually named rooms, each with an en-suite shower room, welcome tray, smart television and Wi-Fi. Choose a harbour outlook or the garden; tell us superking or twin when you reserve.

items.name: Luskentyre
items.alt: The Luskentyre room with a sofa, desk, patterned curtains and a window looking across the harbour to the Harris hills.
items.description: Our super-sized room looks over the North Harbour and Harris hills on one side, and the mature garden and South Harbour on the other. A desk and sofa give you space to spread out a map—or do nothing with the afternoon.
items.distinct: Two outlooks: North Harbour and Harris hills; garden and South Harbour.

items.name: Scarista
items.alt: The bright Scarista room with green armchairs, a writing desk and harbour views through tall windows.
items.description: Large and bright, with elevated views over the harbour and the North Harris hills. Local artwork warms the room, and an extra-large en-suite shower room gives the day’s salt and weather somewhere to stay behind.
items.distinct: Elevated harbour views, local artwork and an extra-large en-suite.

items.name: Borve
items.alt: The Borve room with a double bed, armchairs and a window over the guest house garden.
items.description: Our standard double is still larger than most, with a view over the mature garden towards the South Harbour. It is the quieter choice for guests who prefer green things to blue things—though both are close.
items.distinct: A garden outlook towards the South Harbour, at the standard-room rate.
features: Garden view towards the South Harbour

included: Smart television with FreeSat and streaming

house.title: An open house, in every sense.
house.intro: The address is Victorian. The instinct to welcome a stranger is older.

story.title: A knock at the farmstead door
paragraphs: At dawn on 30 April 1746, Bonnie Prince Charlie and his party arrived by rowing boat from Benbecula. They had disguised themselves as a shipwrecked merchant crew; the Prince was using the name Sinclair. Donald Campbell and his wife knew who their visitors were.

Donald was loyal to the Hanoverian crown and aware of the £30,000 bounty. He chose hospitality anyway: a warm fire, beds, food, shelter and the use of his boat. When a local minister arrived with men to claim the reward, Donald’s answer was plain: “He came to me for safety, so how can I betray him.”

The Prince stayed four nights, leaving on 4 May while a boat was secured in Stornoway for his escape to France. Donald later had to go into hiding. A plaque on the wall commemorates the refuge given on this site.

story.title: Granite, groceries and a manse
paragraphs: The house that stands here today was rebuilt in the 1880s, incorporating the ruins and foundations of Donald Campbell’s farmstead. It has solid granite walls and a prominent position between Scalpay’s North and South Harbours.

It became a draper’s and grocer’s, then a Church Manse, and more recently Two Harbours Guest House. The brief names the granite walls and the earlier foundations; it does not inventory the surviving interior features. [Original interior features to be confirmed by the owner]

story.title: The same open door
paragraphs: The renovation keeps the historic charm and adds modern comforts: three en-suite rooms, a farmhouse kitchen, a mature garden and a guest patio looking over the dry stone wall to the North Harbour and the Harris hills.

The house history calls this a tradition of an ‘open house’. We have kept the story specific because it is specific: a named host, a hunted guest, four nights, and a decision that still explains the welcome.

house.plaque: On this site was the house in which Bonnie Prince Charlie passed some of his days as a fugitive in his own rightful land.
house.alt: An earlier exterior view of Two Harbours, showing the white-painted house, garden, dry stone wall and harbour.

gettingHere.title: The last seven miles are the easy part.
gettingHere.intro: Scalpay is joined to Harris by bridge, so there is no island ferry to catch for the final leg. From Tarbert ferry port, it is a seven-mile scenic drive to the house—about ten minutes.

steps.title: Reach Harris
steps.text: Tarbert is the ferry port and hub of Harris. [Ferry routes, operators, crossing times and booking links to be confirmed]

steps.title: Cross to Scalpay
steps.text: Leave Tarbert on the road across Scalpay Bridge. The bridge connects Scalpay to Harris, joining the three islands of Scalpay, Harris and Lewis.

steps.title: Arrive at the house
steps.text: The house is between the island’s North and South Harbours. Check-in is from 4.30pm to 6.30pm; other times are by arrangement. Tell us if you will arrive after 6.30pm so we can be there to meet you.
